### 🐛 Describe the bug

Summary

Serving Kimi-K3 with TP16 across two 8× B200 nodes (EFA, no NVSwitch/MNNVL),any form of CUDA graph capture produces wrong output or crashes. enforce_eager is correct 100% of the time. Unlike #50147, this reproduces at batch=1 on the first request, with prefix caching disabled and no concurrency. I also tried TP=8 and PP=2, the issue persists

Critically, the FlashInfer fused all-reduce path is disabled on this topology, so the latent-MoE stale-residual fix in #50386 cannot apply here (details below).

Configuration

vllm serve flags:

  • -tensor-parallel-size 16 --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors
    --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA
    --disable-custom-all-reduce --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune
    --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90

env: VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0
VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0
VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=0

Prefix caching is OFF. All tests below are single-stream, temperature=0, max_tokens=64, identical prompt.

Failure matrix

cudagraph config | result -- | -- enforce_eager: true | Correct output, every time, across many deploys (TP16 and TP8+PP2) default (FULL_AND_PIECEWISE) | Fluent but semantically random multilingual text; host SIGSEGV in cuGraphLaunch / at::cuda::CUDAGraph::replay() on the 3rd request cudagraph_mode: PIECEWISE | No crash. Deterministic collapse to a single repeated token (@ @ @ ...) from the first request VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 | AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered, surfaced at torch.cuda.set_rng_state during Dynamo tracing

Performance impact

Eager decode is ~2.6 tok/s at batch=1 (64 tokens in ~25 s), closely matching the ~2.7 tok/s eager figure in #50147 against ~85 tok/s with graphs. DSpark speculative decoding recovers this to ~10 tok/s, still far below the graph-enabled figure. Eager is therefore not a viable workaround for latency-sensitive serving, which makes graph capture on this topology effectively blocking.

Questions

  1. Is CUDA graph capture expected to be supported for Kimi-K3 on multi-node TP without NVSwitch, where the FlashInfer fused all-reduce path is inactive and collectives fall back to NCCL over EFA? But I tried TP=8 and PP=2 the issue still persist.
  2. Are there other buffers allocated outside capture in the K3 MoE/KDA paths, analogous to the one fixed in #50386, that would be reached on the non-FlashInfer path?

Reproduction

Serve:

vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 --nnodes 2 --node-rank $RANK \
  --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA \
  --disable-custom-all-reduce --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90
# env:
#   VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0
#   VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0
#   VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=0
# Add --enforce-eager for the known-good control run.

Single request, greedy, no concurrency:

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="<http://localhost:8000/v1>", api_key="dummy", timeout=600.0)
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="moonshotai/Kimi-K3",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "can you write me a story about a cat"}],
    max_tokens=64,
    temperature=0,
    extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking": False}},
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

With --enforce-eager this returns a coherent story on every run. Without it, the first response is already corrupted. Send the same request 3+ times to reach the segfault under the default cudagraph mode.
